In this study, we examine how to establish an unambiguous and systematic assessment of harm caused by autonomous systems by considering a specific task: measuring the negative impact of autonomous vehicle navigation. To tackle this problem, we develop a model that integrates probability, topology, and time: the causal path harm graph (CPH^2). By incorporating key CP^2 elements, such as social linkages and temporal frames, a more comprehensive characterization of harm is gained, which can be applied to any CP^2-fitted evaluation framework. We showcase our approach using Bremen, Germany as a case study and introduce an open-source tool for analyzing potential social harm caused by autonomous vehicle navigation in town. Our framework's versatility allows it to be adapted for assessing various types of autonomous system failures. Furthermore, we present an easy-to-use software platform, HARMASCHUND, which utilizes the Bremen evaluation framework to facilitate assessments from the perspective of relevant stakeholders. By demonstrating its practical applications, we aim to encourage utilization of this tool in real-world scenarios. As autonomous systems continue to shape our society, integrating HARMASCHUND into the decision-making process can aid in identifying and mitigating potential social harm. The software platform and evaluation framework may also be expanded to other types of applications. HARMASCHUND's capabilities can be utilized via its public web interface at harmaschund.de. In the future, integrating assessments based on HARMASCHUND through an open-source blockchain, such as the Hyperledger Fabric framework, could enhance their reliability and applicability in real-world contexts. All project-related code and HARMASCHUND assessments are available for free on our public GitHub repository at github.com/harmaschund. By undertaking this research, we aim to contribute to existing discussions on autonomous system failure assessment and introduce a new approach to measuring harm. By expanding on this topic, we aim to encourage more researchers and practitioners to examine the various forms of autonomous system failure. Conventional two-stage approaches using speech recognition and machine translation have inherent flaws, including the amplification of inaccuracies. By combining speech recognition and machine translation into a singular model, zero-shot translation eliminates the need for additional training data, but current models still struggle with rare words in target languages. Furthermore, we demonstrate that a two-way model can successfully translate speech-to-text without direct examples, outperforming various one-way models and approaches that rely on speech recognition and machine translation. In the field of legged locomotion, spring-based actuators can boost energy efficiency and performance but complicate the controller's design. We diverge from conventional methods of developing optimal controllers through in-depth modeling and simulation. Instead, our controller generation strategy mimics nature by adapting central pattern generator concepts to produce spring-assisted gaits in a more automated manner. The key components of our neural-like controller, consisting of a low-dimensional state estimator and gauge-bond regulation, enable gaits to emerge without the comprehensive mathematical models typically required. We successfully test and validate this controller on the Suzy II quadruped robot and explore the controller's adaptability and underlying parameters. Experimental findings indicate that our controller, operating without precise models, achieves gaits comparable to those generated by conventional optimization methods. The research demonstrates that CPG-inspired controller generation can result in efficient, high-performance gaits in systems equipped with spring actuators. Moreover, it's evident that such a controller can effectively produce gaits in real-time, relying solely on sensor data, and is less dependent on comprehensive system models. The controller's relative simplicity is highlighted by its low computational requirements during operation. Finally, we investigate the controller's robustness and examine its behavior under simulated and real-world disturbances, verifying that it accommodates a range of spriging scenarios. The research ultimately contributes to the development of adaptable, spring-assisted gaits in legged robots across diverse applications and ground conditions. The corresponding controller generation strategy may also accelerate the spring-equipped gaits exploration in robotics field. A surge in demand for search by image has led researchers to investigate fashion instance-level image retrieval, which involves finding matching images. Building upon this, the concept of fashion attribute manipulation, which modifies a specific attribute while retaining others, has emerged. This enables users to search not only identical items but also similar items with specific attributes. However, this task is challenging due to the difficulty in defining attributes and preserving query uniqueness. Although fashion instance-level image retrieval and fashion attribute manipulation are crucial in real-world applications, most studies have focused on one problem alone. In this research, we aim to achieve state-of-the-art results on both tasks. To accomplish this, we propose a novel method that translates a query into a feature space, preserving query uniqueness by modulating a specified attribute. By employing contrastive learning, our approach promotes query uniqueness while retaining information on the desired attribute through soft attribute manipulation. We experimentally validate our method, demonstrating its ability to excel in both image retrieval tasks and demonstrating its advantage over existing methods on two benchmark datasets. We anticipate that our method will contribute significantly to the field by achieving state-of-the-art results on the Fashion-UIR dataset and achieving a top-10 accuracy on the UIR-FAM task on the UIR dataset. The contribution of our method will be further supported by a comprehensive analysis of its evaluation metrics, as well as an interactive visualization tool that showcases its capability to search for manipulated queries by interacting with a fixed query feature. We anticipate that our code along with the evaluation tool will become publicly available. Furthermore, we propose two additional datasets, namely, the Fashion-UIR-FAM and ApparelUIR-C, which will further facilitate a comparison of our method with other approaches. We anticipate that our work will serve as a foundation for future advancements in fashion attribute manipulation by introducing novel evaluation metrics and dataset annotations. Furthermore, we anticipate that our work will contribute to the field of code and benchmarking by making our code and benchmarking materials openly available. Constructing the matching cost is a critical step in estimating light field depth but is often performed using the block-SAD constructor, which is computationally intensive. This incompatibility limits the practical application of light field technology, particularly in areas requiring fast frame rates. To overcome this challenge, a novel matching cost constructor called BoSAD is proposed to efficiently calculate the matching cost for light fields. This constructor can be seamlessly integrated into various deep neural network architectures, such as SSLF, to facilitate high-quality light field depth estimation. When compared to its counterparts, BoSAD delivers a substantial reduction of 55% to 65% in terms of computational cost, while achieving comparable or even improved estimation accuracy. This innovative constructor is now made available to the public in the hope of advancing light field research and facilitating the development of faster and more advanced technologies. The constructor can be accessed via the following link: https://github.com/HiwangBo/SimpleCostConstructor. When used in conjunction with the SSLF network, our proposed constructor achieves superior results on the standard 7D dataset, yielding an estimated 0.0231 to 0.0261 anisotropic depth gradient values. Conversely, when applied to the higher-dimensional datasets, our method exhibits a slight decrease in performance due to the challenges posed by large occlusion areas. Given this limitation, a comprehensive comparison of our constructor, including its performance on the DSA, FLIR AD, and LLFF datasets, is presented. On the DSA dataset, our constructor demarcates regions prone to occlusions with a substantial accuracy rate of 92.6% (benchmark: 90.6%). The increasing use of high-bandwidth applications such as online gaming, virtual reality, and high-definition video streaming require networks with enhanced throughput levels and reduced latency. One effective strategy for achieving these goals is to deploy multiple access points within a given area, but this is often hindered by the need to balance network resource distribution with minimal over-lap of coverage areas. Some of these topological structures include the deployment of large-scale backhauls and smaller links at the edge, featuring fully connected central hubs and mesh links within the periphery. By focusing on the role of hierarchical link hierarchy in these systems, an approach has been developed in which network links are represented as digraphs where edge weights reflect the links' hierarchical order. The proposed method has been explored through both theoretical analysis and simulations, revealing its potential benefits and limitations. Initial results indicate that this approach can enhance network throughput levels while minimizing network link occupancy.
